situation.note: made redundant at 52 after 25 years. I'm not short of money. I'm short of a reason to get up. who am I if I'm not that job.

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call searching for what it's all for, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: From 'who am I without that job' to 'who am I beyond every role', over seven days of reading and sitting.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the loss of shape and the question, without rushing to fix it.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that meaning is not in the role, and the self is not the work.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what you are cannot be lost, and it was there before the job and will be after.
week_beats.act: You sit with one verse a day and ask the question of yourself without an answer.
week_beats.story: A man who lost his name and kingdom is asked who he is, and answers with what he was not.

understanding.core_struggle: A man after years in one role, is searching for a reason to get up and wondering who he is without it.
understanding.mirror: The money is there, and the morning is not.
understanding.insight: Nothing is exactly wrong, and that's the hard part. You've outgrown the reasons that used to carry you.
understanding.mechanism_label: Searching for what it's all for

situations.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful
I can't handle not knowing what comes next
I want to reconnect with my roots

queries.hook: The morning has lost its shape after years in one role, and the question is who you are beyond it.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be lost; it is not the role you held, not the title, not the work. It is what was there before and will be after.
queries.act: Sit with the question, read one verse a day, and ask it of yourself without rushing to an answer.
queries.story: A man who lost his kingdom and his name, and was asked who he was, answered with what he was not.

weeks: The one who was never the role

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
verse.line: What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.
verse.translation: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; and where all beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna what a steady person is like. Krishna answers by describing someone who stays awake while the crowd sleeps, and who sees past what the crowd chases. The verse says that what looks like night to everyone else is the time for the self-controlled to be awake. It means that steadiness is built by guarding your attention. When you dwell on things, anger begins and leads to ruin.
verse.for_you: Turn inward, come to know the self, and let your work become service and offering; a life lived from there is full.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you are awake to today that the old crowd would have slept through.
verse.scene_line: You stand awake in the crowd's night, with no one to name what you see.
asks: What am I awake to now?
Where does my attention rest when no one is watching?
What is the crowd chasing that I can already see past?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: रात्रिः सैव पुनः स एव दिवसो मत्वा मुधा जन्तवो धावन्त्युद्यमिनस्तथैव निभृतप्रारब्धतत्तत्क्रियाः । व्यापारैः पुनरुक्तभूत विषयैरित्थंविधेनामुना संसारेण कदर्थिता वयमहो मोहान्न लज्जामहे ॥
verse.line: Same night, same day, the same tasks on repeat. We run in circles and call it living.
verse.translation: Thinking 'it is the same night again, the same day', creatures run about in vain, busy as ever with the tasks they have set going; with work full of the same repeated things, tormented by this round of existence, alas, out of delusion we feel no shame.
verse.why: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
prasang.summary: Time empties cities, houses and courts; the busy never notice it passing; parents and childhood friends become memories. The section ends with life as a play and death as the curtain.
prasang.lesson: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari wrote this for the reader, sitting with the sense that life is repeating itself. He saw creatures running through the same night and the same day, caught in tasks they set going themselves. They are busy, but the work is full of the same repeated things. He says they are tormented by this round, yet out of delusion they feel no shame. The point is that time is passing while you are busy. Notice it before it is gone.
verse.for_you: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
verse.try_today: Notice one task you do that repeats without thought, and let it go today.
verse.scene_line: You are in the same room where the work used to be, and the day is ending again.
asks: How do I notice time without it feeling like a loss?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha's closing advice to Rama on living in the world after the three vows.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
verse.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
verse.translation: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is finishing his counsel to Rama. He tells Rama to stay anchored within while doing all the outer work that comes to you. He means that if you turn your attention inward and rest there, you will never grow weary. You can do everything you are asked to do, but you will not burn out, because you will not be trapped by the sense that you are the one doing it. The idea is to work fully, enjoy fully, and let go fully, anchored inside, so that the outer work does not consume you.
verse.for_you: Nothing is exactly wrong, and that's the hard part. You've outgrown the reasons that used to carry you.
verse.try_today: Notice what is still here when the work voice is quiet.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting in the quiet after the work has left, and the question is whether you can still be anchored within.
asks: How do I know the inner anchor is still holding?
How do I let go of the sense of being the one who does?

verse.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
verse.setting: On the self in the heart that we visit nightly in deep sleep without knowing it.
verse.sanskrit: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
verse.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
verse.translation: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

verse.meaning: A teacher once told a reader that the self in the heart is visited every night in deep sleep. Like people walking daily over buried gold without knowing the spot, they pass their own treasure and never find it. This happens because they are carried away by untruth. The idea is that you are already whole. You do not need to find a new self. You just need to stop walking over it.
verse.for_you: You are walking over a hidden treasure. The job was a path, not the destination. The search for a new reason is the untruth. What you are looking for is already here. Your own worth is the ground beneath your feet.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing today that you do without needing a reason to do it.
verse.scene_line: You are walking over your own buried gold, not knowing the spot.
asks: How do I know what is my treasure and what is just noise?
Who am I when I am not looking for a reason?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
verse.sanskrit: विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः । विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
verse.line: Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give your full attention to one thing.
verse.translation: Sitting in a quiet place, senses at rest, self-mastered, pure within, one should contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the Self.
verse.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

verse.meaning: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion. Rama tells him to sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, and give his full attention to one thing. The idea is that quiet sitting and steady faith carry a person until understanding becomes natural. It is not about forcing answers. It is about letting the mind settle like a still ocean, so the truth can surface on its own.
verse.for_you: The redundancy came and the structure left. Now the hours open up, but they do not always feel like freedom. You are searching for a reason to get up, and the old reasons no longer fit.
verse.try_today: Sit in a quiet place and let your senses rest for five minutes.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet of your own life, waiting for the next thing to name you.
asks: How do I give my full attention to one thing when I feel adrift?
What is the one thing I can rest my attention on today?

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram, now king, speaks to the people about the human life they have.
verse.sanskrit: फिरत सदा माया कर प्रेरा। काल कर्म सुभाव गुन घेरा॥ कबहुँक करि करुना नर देही। देत ईस बिनु हेतु सनेही ॥ नर तनु भव बारिधि कहुँ बेरो। सन्मुख मरुत अनुग्रह मेरो॥ करनधार सदगुर दृढ़ नावा। दुर्लभ साज सुलभ करि पावा ॥
verse.line: This life is the boat, my grace the wind behind it, a good teacher at the helm.
verse.translation: Driven always by illusion, surrounded by time, karma, nature and the qualities, the soul wanders; then sometimes, out of compassion, God, a friend without a reason, gives it a human body. The human body is a boat for the ocean of becoming, my grace is the favourable wind, a true teacher is the steady helmsman: you have been given, easily, what is hard to get.

verse.meaning: Ram speaks to the citizens of Ayodhya. He tells them that the soul wanders through illusion and time, but that God grants a human body out of compassion. This body is a boat crossing the ocean of existence. My grace is the wind, and a true teacher is the helmsman. You have been given, easily, what is hard to get.
verse.for_you: Nothing is exactly wrong, and that's the hard part. You've outgrown the reasons that used to carry you.
verse.try_today: Sit by a window for five minutes, and give your full attention to the one sound you hear.
verse.scene_line: You are at the helm of your own boat, with the wind at your back, and you are just beginning to steer.
asks: How do I know when I am steering and not just drifting?
What is the one thing I can see without needing to fix it?
Who is the teacher I am waiting for in this quiet?

story.title: King Brihadratha's despair
story.story_hook: King Brihadratha had everything a king could want, and walked away from all of it.
story.summary: A king hands his throne to his son and goes to the forest, overwhelmed by how everything decays. When a sage offers him a wish, he says he feels like a frog in a dark well and asks to be shown the way out.
story.lesson: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.

anchor.speaker: King Brihadratha
anchor.setting: The king's plea after listing everything that passes.
anchor.sanskrit: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥
anchor.line: Like a frog in a dark well, I am stuck in this life. Show me the way out.
anchor.translation: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
anchor.why: Even success can leave you feeling stuck; asking for help is the first step out.

prasang.story_hook: King Brihadratha had everything a king could want, and walked away from all of it.

story.hook_title: A king who had everything still felt like a frog in a dark well
story.teaser: A king who had everything still felt like a frog in a dark well
story.for_you: You have walked away from your throne and now sit in a forest of your own, watching the old world decay around you. The question is no longer how to rule, but how to see the light again. What you were not is now your truest ground.
asks: How do I ask for a way out without knowing what the way looks like?
Who am I when the kingdom is gone?
